trails.name: White Trail
trails.description: Official 4.0-mile out-and-back and the easiest hiking route on the west side. From the West Launch it follows the lakeshore, rolls through the agricultural fields and horse-barn area, and reaches the dam. Wide, largely gentle tread with a few short climbs.

trails.name: Blue Trail
trails.description: Official 3.5-mile loop with blue blazes, rated more difficult. Mostly wooded and wide enough for horses, it passes historic ruins and follows the East Branch of the Brandywine Creek on the park's west edge.

trails.name: Green Trail
trails.description: Official 1.0-mile connector with green blazes, rated more difficult. It links the West Launch area to the Blue Trail so riders and hikers can build a longer wooded loop.

trails.name: Lime Loop
trails.description: Official 1.8-mile loop with lime blazes, rated more difficult. The loop branches off the Blue Trail in the northwestern part of the park and is a local favorite for mountain biking and horseback riding.

trails.name: Mansion Trails
trails.description: Official 0.9-mile connector with white/blue blazes, rated easiest. Stone foundations and other remnants of the village of Milford Mills, flooded when the reservoir filled, sit beside the path.

trails.name: Park Road Trail
trails.description: Official 0.6-mile out-and-back, rated easiest and the park's ADA route. The paved path runs from the boat-rental parking area past the warm-season grass fields to the accessible fishing pier at the East Launch.

trails.name: Red Trail
trails.description: Official 1.5-mile loop with red blazes, rated more difficult and open to hiking only. It is the east-side trail, running along the lake and through woods between the day-use areas and the East Launch.

trails.name: Yellow Trail
trails.description: Official 6.2-mile out-and-back with yellow blazes, rated most difficult. It starts at the Dorlan Mill Road parking area and threads the mountain-bike loops south and east of the dam, with steep pitches, roots and rock.

pois.name: West Launch Lake Vista
pois.description: Open view across the main basin from the west boat launch, with the north arm stretching away to the left and the dam far to the southeast.
pois.alertText: Look left — the lake opens up beyond the launch

pois.name: Marsh Creek Dam Overlook
pois.description: The 90-foot-high, 990-foot-long earth-and-rock fill dam closes the south end of the lake. The dam was built between 1970 and 1973.
pois.alertText: Ahead — the 990-foot dam holding back 535 acres of water

pois.name: North Arm Overlook
pois.description: The reservoir narrows into a winding north arm here, with drowned timber and quiet backwater habitat toward Little Conestoga Road.
pois.alertText: Look left — the north arm winds away toward the woods

pois.name: East Launch Marina View
pois.description: Sailboats, rental craft and seasonal mooring slips fill the east basin beside the boat rental and snack bar.
pois.alertText: Marina ahead — watch for sailboats crossing the basin

pois.name: Milford Mills Ruins
pois.description: Stone foundations and cellar holes mark the village of Milford Mills, the only settlement inside the area flooded for the reservoir.
pois.alertText: Historic stone foundations on your left — Milford Mills

pois.name: Murphy Mansion Site
pois.description: Mike Murphy's 168-acre racehorse estate, including a 44-room mansion, once formed almost the whole village. The buildings were demolished during park development.
pois.alertText: Murphy Mansion site — a 44-room house stood here

pois.name: Larkin Covered Bridge Site
pois.description: An 1854 covered bridge once spanned Marsh Creek at Milford Mills. It was moved to an Upper Uwchlan Township trail before the valley was flooded.
pois.alertText: The 1854 Larkin covered bridge once crossed here

pois.name: Dam Construction Interpretive Site
pois.description: Construction ran from May 1970 to June 1973. The gates closed on November 16, 1973, and the lake reached normal pool on June 21, 1974.
pois.alertText: 1970s dam works — the gates closed in November 1973

pois.name: Heron Rookery
pois.description: Drowned snags in the quiet north arm give herons and other wading birds a sheltered nesting and feeding area in spring.
pois.alertText: Heron rookery on the north arm — quiet please

pois.name: Osprey Platform
pois.description: Ospreys are regular spring and fall migrants over the lake and rebuild stick nests on platform poles near the east shore.
pois.alertText: Osprey platform ahead — look up and scan the sky

pois.name: Bald Eagle Perch
pois.description: Bald eagles patrol the open water here, especially in winter when migrating waterfowl concentrate on the lake.
pois.alertText: Bald eagle often perches in the tall oak on the point

pois.name: Turtle Basking Platforms
pois.description: The lake's artificial fish-habitat program includes turtle basking platforms; painted and snapping turtles haul out on warm afternoons.
pois.alertText: Count the turtles on the basking platforms

pois.name: Grassland Bird Meadow
pois.description: Warm-season grasses of Indian grass, big and little bluestem and switchgrass shelter bobolinks, meadowlarks, savannah sparrows and northern harriers.
pois.alertText: Listen — bobolinks and meadowlarks nest in this grass

pois.name: Wood Duck Cove
pois.description: A sheltered cove off the east basin where wood ducks, mallards and spring migrants loaf in the flooded brush.
pois.alertText: Quiet cove on the right — wood ducks frequent the brush

pois.name: Dam Spillway
pois.description: The concrete spillway carries releases around the earth-fill dam into Marsh Creek and the East Branch Brandywine downstream.

pois.name: East Branch Brandywine
pois.description: The East Branch of the Brandywine Creek threads the western woods and feeds the reservoir; the Blue Trail follows its bank.
pois.alertText: Creek crossing ahead — the East Branch of the Brandywine

pois.name: ADA Fishing Pier
pois.description: The accessible fishing pier at the East Launch has ADA parking nearby and is the destination of the paved Park Road Trail.
pois.alertText: Accessible fishing pier ahead — level paved approach

pois.name: Sunset Point
pois.description: A west-shore opening with an unobstructed sightline down the lake toward the dam — the park's classic evening photograph.
pois.alertText: Sunset Point — arrive 30 minutes before dusk

pois.name: Butterfly Meadow
pois.description: A planted meadow of native warm-season flowers beside the west fields, best for macro photography from July through September.
pois.alertText: Photo stop — butterfly meadow in bloom on your right
